keyVerseText: And I will bring a sword upon you, that shall avenge the quarrel of my covenant: and when ye are gathered together within your cities, I will send the pestilence among you; and ye shall be delivered into the hand of the enemy.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun נָקָם (nâqâm) derives from the root verb נָקַם (nâqam), which fundamentally means to avenge, punish, or take revenge. This root conveys the idea of actively responding to wrong or injury, often with a sense of retributive justice. Beyond the English glosses of 'vengeance' or 'revenge,' the root emphasizes a deliberate and rightful act of setting things right, often by God or an agent acting on His behalf.
usageInScripture: The word נָקָם appears 17 times in the Hebrew Bible, primarily translated as 'vengeance' in 8 instances, with other renderings including 'of vengeance' and 'the quarrel.' Its usage consistently relates to the concept of retributive justice, whether enacted by God, human agents like Samson, or Israel’s enemies. This range shows that נָקָם carries both divine and human dimensions of avenging wrongs, highlighting its role in covenantal justice and conflict resolution.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding נָקָם enriches our grasp of God's justice as both holy and righteous retribution against sin and covenant violation. It reminds believers that God alone holds the ultimate right to avenge, a truth that calls for trust in His perfect judgment rather than personal retaliation. This word underscores the seriousness of sin and the certainty of divine justice, pointing forward to Christ who bore the penalty for our offenses, thus satisfying God's righteous vengeance on our behalf. Recognizing נָקָם invites believers to rest in God's sovereign justice and mercy, fostering humility and faith.
keyVerseReflection: Leviticus 26:25 states, 'And I will bring a sword upon you, that shall avenge the quarrel of my covenant,' highlighting God's direct intervention to uphold His covenantal holiness. The use of נָקָם here conveys that God's punishment is not arbitrary but a measured response to covenant breach, executing justice to vindicate His name. This verse reveals that divine vengeance serves to maintain the integrity of God's relationship with His people, warning of consequences yet also affirming God's faithfulness to His covenant promises.
